title: Part IV without the item slide: Melee dock ghost, Low Street spectre, High Street, church, LeChuck close-up, Stan's fight, ending (DOS CD, SCUMM v5)

entry.notes: First frame of the 'Last Part' card: room 95, loaded by global/script-131.txt [0039]. 131 is started by room-070-hellcliff/local-206.txt [046E], right after startScript(17,[2]) (verbs back) and UserputOn at [0464]-[046C]. 131 itself sets Bit[453] (Part IV) at [002F] and Var[277] = 6 at [0034]. This is the no-slide S6's last target ({room: 95}, routes/anypercent/noslide/S6.json). NO STEP OF PART IV USES THE ITEM SLIDE. No slide survives into Part IV (the UserputOn above). None can be formed either: each dialogue choice runs UserputOff (global/script-014.txt [00E2]) and then script 32's UserputOn (global/script-032.txt [0011]). The only 'gate: input' moves below are the two fireworks menus, which global 138 itself draws inside its own cutscene with input on (see goals 13-14); they are the game's normal way to answer, not a slide. FACTS S7 NEEDS FROM S6 AND CANNOT REPAIR: (1) ego owns 823, the root beer ('magic seltzer bottle', global/script-106.txt [055B]), with class 6 cleared ([0573] setClass(823,[6,146])); room-078-church/entry.txt [000E]-[0027] starts the wedding script local 201 only if ego owns it, and 823's Use handler (room-075-gh-hull/obj-0823-voodoo-root.txt [00A7]) only passes the sentence on while class 6 is clear. (2) Bit[51] == 1 (Stan's first visit, global/script-056.txt [3F04]). Without it, room-059-stans/entry.txt [0035]-[004C] starts Stan's sales script local 201 on top of global 133's fight (Stan is in room 0 and Var[196] >= 3). (3) Var[196] == 3: High Street starts no wandering pirates (room-034-high-stre/entry.txt [0067]). (4) var 19 == 5 (the logo glitch): every frame count below assumes 12 frames/s. STATE THAT DOES NOT MATTER: (a) state(438), the church door: 0 by default, and goal 6 opens it; if a Part I wandering pirate left it open, goal 6 already holds and is skipped. (b) Bit[436]: the vista catapult with Var[242] == 2 sets it (room-011-vista-1/local-207.txt [002C]). It only switches which line 131 prints at the dock ([00BD]: same two segments either way) and the ending cutaway (global/script-138.txt [0358], global/script-146.txt [0000]). No target reads it. Bits 455, 468, 537 and 565 are 0 (set only in Part IV). On the first room-83 frame the inventory is cut down to 823, 488 and 733 (room-083-cu-dock/entry.txt [0020]-[0067], Var[277] == 6), so whatever Part III's normal solutions left in the inventory does not matter. THE CARD LASTS 129.8 s (CD track 6, sound 107: global/script-131.txt [0059]-[0060]), about 7794 ticks = about 1559 frames at VAR_TIMER_NEXT 5. It is a cutscene with no override, so Esc does nothing. Goal 1's hint waits it out with a 'delay' (see there).

goals.note: NEW GOAL. The old file claimed ego could reach archway 451 at y <= 120 while x < 299, and so avoid the spectre. Room 35's walk boxes rule that out. Ego enters at (437,107), in box 21. The box matrix's only way to 451's walk point (160,88), in box 1, is 21 -> 7 -> 6 -> 5 -> 4 -> 3 -> 2 -> 1. Box 6 (x 299-467, y 127-141) meets box 4 (bottom edge y 124, x 47-290) only through box 5 (x 48-299, y 124-141), so every walk to 451 passes x < 299 with y >= 124. local 212 (freeze-resistant) then stops ego and starts the spectre's dialogue 211.
